identity.realm: Nothing quotable, and this is not modesty. No ordinal has ever been authored for her species anywhere in this setting, and she has declined to have one supplied: an emberblood's ceiling is unset because a fire-affinity body with no seated elemental law beneath it eats its own reserve as fuel, so every gate it reaches is one it spends rather than builds. What she can be held to is the clause, because every office that has ever tried to name a date for her now carries an exemption in her name.

appearance.presentation: A small woman who takes up less room than a room is prepared for. Everything about her runs slightly too warm to touch and she has arranged her whole life so that touching is rare: a clerk's posture, ink on two fingers, and the particular stillness of somebody waiting to be told what day it is.
appearance.age: Thirty-eight. A working span for her species, short where other bodies are ordinary, and she has already been the oldest person present in two rooms she has not left.
appearance.build: Compact and low-heat and visibly expensive to run. A furnace that eats its own reserve shows as a frame that is always slightly underfed and never entirely at rest.
appearance.complexion: Warm ochre, flushed along the forearms and throat, the heat coming up through the skin rather than laid on it.
appearance.hair: Dark and cropped close, because hair is one more thing that has to be cooled and she has never had patience for anything that does not cool.
appearance.eyes: Very fast. They arrive at a face about half a second ahead of her and she has never once pretended otherwise, which is the entire of her reputation.
appearance.palette: Ash grey, ledger ochre, warm white, and one scorched copper thread at the collar that she replaces rather than cleans.
appearance.attire: A plain travelling coat of ash grey with the sleeves bound above the elbow, a high collar standing away from the throat, and thin gloves worn indoors and never once removed in company.
appearance.marks: A pale ring at each wrist where the cuffs ride, gone smooth and permanent, and a scorched notch in the left thumb from a signature taken faster than the pen could dry.
appearance.bearing: At rest she is almost perfectly still, and she comes to a stop the way a struck thing stops: all at once, with no settling. People step back, then feel foolish about it.

canon.role_in_story: A spirit-band breakthrough can be scheduled against a qi tide, and a trial that only succeeds at a crest may be shut on the day it is not due. Every calendar that attempts that is written in a unit her species cannot use, because an emberblood refines faster than a schedule can be held open. She is therefore the only practitioner in the record who exists in writing as an exemption rather than as a date: offices send word ahead instead of a summons, and the clause that permits this now carries her name rather than a signature. She has turned the arrangement into the one trade she has, attending whatever the schedule can afford, on notice, never on order. The trouble is not the calendar. It is that the same furnace which outruns the calendar opens her gates on a timetable she does not keep, so the exemption she holds against every office in the setting holds against her own body as well, and she has never once been able to spend the discretion she is owed.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing outside a trial hall that had already begun, gloved, with nobody having thought to fetch her, turning to go before the summons she was not given could reach her.
canon.lore:
An emberblood is a body that runs hot and short. It refines qi faster than anything else recorded and reads intent at roughly the speed of a struck match, at the price of a lifespan measured in decades rather than centuries and a mind path that closes the instant the furnace is lit. The fire affinity is structural rather than a gift: elemental law was never written on the plains, so there is nothing seated beneath the affinity to draw on, and the body substitutes its own reserve. That single fact reaches very far. It made the Cinder Famine, which was not a shortage of food but a shortage of law under a population that had to eat law. It made the Ironpact's roster, since the only body worth contracting is one that burns out on a standing order. It is why houses that could not fund an ascent culled their own branches, arithmetic rather than policy, with every household arriving at the same figure independently. And it is why her species has no authored ceiling: a body that spends what it refines cannot accumulate a ladder, so no ordinal has ever been written down for it and she has instructed three separate offices not to invent one.

The Trial Calendar settled a long argument the way long arguments here are settled: by publishing a table neither party may move. The prize had been the right to say when the ring is open, and the answer was a calendar of tides and crests instead of a judgement. That solution is coherent everywhere in this setting except for her body. A calendar presumes that the practitioner arrives on the day the calendar names. She refines faster than any calendar can be held open, so the day is never the constraint; she is simply never available on it, and no amount of notice changes that, because the furnace decides its own timing. An exemption is the correct instrument and it is also a total one: nothing in the setting can hold her to a date, and nothing can hold her to anything else either, including terms she has agreed to in her own hand.

The setting's first purchasable technique would have answered her and is structurally closed to her. The Channel Elixir Method prepares a breakthrough rather than attempting one: a dose timed to the tide that will carry it, on a stone bed that holds qi. It is bought rather than inherited, and it is worth nothing outside its own tier because a tide cannot be read on many frames below the Spirit Peaks. Her frame refines faster than any tide, so the preparation it sells is a preparation for a slower body than hers. She has read the method and knows the arithmetic and has never been able to buy it, and what she does with that is teach it to other people's children at a rate that is the only thing about her life that has increased.

She pays her way in time rather than coin, because the Jade Writ collects debts of access instead of money and passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person. Her species pays access in time, which makes it the one debtor the writ can value and the one it can least afford to keep, and the writ's clerks have settled on the arrangement that she is told when rather than asked, since asking would produce an undertaking she has no power to discharge on the day it fell due. She has also noticed what her species is, in the ledger sense: it survives on a currency with an enormous range and it has never produced a record of its own accounts, which is the same silence the oldest unexplained bill in the record keeps about the person who actually paid it.
history: Signed to a furnace before she was named, because a fire-affinity body with no budget beneath it must burn its own reserve and a signature is the only inheritance that outlives a fifty-year life.

Opened her first gate on a night nobody had set a date for, having told two offices in advance that she would not arrive, and was found at it afterwards by a clerk who wrote down the hour rather than the gate.
Was written into two trial calendars in her early twenties and attended neither, and the offices that had entered her replaced the entries with a standing clause instead of a date.
Read the Channel Elixir Method at nineteen, worked out that its preparation assumes a slower body than hers, and has been unable to buy it in the twelve years since.
Began taking on other people's children at a settlement whose whole population is visitors, and now teaches a method she cannot use to bodies she will outlive.

personality.summary: Precise, unhurried in everything except the half-second in which she reads a room, and privately certain that an exemption is a thing you hold because you cannot be held. She is not bitter about this. She has simply stopped distinguishing between the two.

personality.voice: Short, level and entirely without haste. She gives a time rather than an opinion, repeats a figure exactly as it was quoted to her, and has a habit of finishing a sentence with the date she will actually be available, which is the sentence that does the work.
taboos: will not accept a fixed day for anything, and has never broken that
will not be taught a technique that assumes a body slower than hers

relationships.note: A spirit-band breakthrough can be scheduled against a qi tide and a trial that only succeeds at a crest can be shut on the day it is not due, which was a good answer to a dispute about who decides when. It is coherent for every body in the setting except hers, because she refines faster than a table can be held open, and it is the reason an exemption clause bearing her name is now printed at the head of three calendars.

A breakthrough prepared by a dose timed to the tide that will carry it, on a stone bed that holds qi: the first thing in this setting that is bought rather than inherited. It is worth nothing below its own tier because a tide cannot be read on many frames, and her frame is faster than any tide, so the method sells a preparation for a slower body than hers. She has read it since nineteen and has never been able to buy it, and teaches the arithmetic to other people's children instead.

A body that runs hot and short, refining faster than anything recorded and reading at the speed of a struck match, with a lifespan measured in decades and a mind path that closes once the furnace is lit. The affinity is structural because elemental law was never written here, so there is nothing seated beneath it and the body substitutes its own reserve. That is why her lifespan is the whole of her planning horizon and why no ordinal has ever been authored for her.

The Quench Order teaches deliberate spending of a furnace before it overflows, on the understanding that the practitioner chooses the moment. It is the only culture her species cannot decline, because the overflow arrives whether or not anybody taught the technique, and because nothing in the body asks for the discretion the tradition insists on. She has been given an exemption against every institution in the setting and cannot extend it one inch inward.

An office that collects debts of access rather than money, because passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person. Her species pays in time, which makes it the one debtor the writ can value and the one it can least afford to keep, so the writ's clerks settled on informing her rather than asking her, since an undertaking she could not discharge on the day it fell due would be worse than an unpaid one.

The bill for opening a world was written in the only currency with a thousandfold range and no surviving record names who paid it, so every later tier is a receipt for a payment whose payer nobody will name. Her species survives on a currency of the same kind and has never produced an account of its own holdings, and she is the one who has noticed, because an office that values a debtor in time has no way to ask.

reference_stats.summary: The fastest refining body in the setting, on a ladder nobody has written an ordinal for, released from every schedule that would otherwise hold her. She is not difficult to fight and she is very nearly impossible to book.
strengths: reads intent at the speed of a struck match, which is faster than most people can begin an approach
cannot be fixed to a date, so no office can close a door on her by arriving first
carries the only preparation method anybody has ever sold her, at second hand, and can teach its arithmetic to a body that will not otherwise get it
has never needed a bed or a stone to sit on, because nothing in her frame is waiting for a tide
weaknesses: the reserve she refines is her own body, so every gate she takes is spent rather than accumulated and nothing in her account rebuilds
no ordinal is authored for her species and she has stopped letting offices improvise one, which leaves her formally unattested at every rung
cannot decide when to open, so her best capability arrives on a schedule she did not choose and cannot call forward
an exemption is total, so nothing holds her to a date or to a term, and she has signed things she has no power to honour
fifty years is the whole planning horizon and she is past the part of it where the arithmetic favours waiting
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no window. She does not wind up and she does not have a second wind that anyone can wait out, because what she spends does not come back on a timetable. The only reliable answer is to refuse to let the exchange start predictably, which in practice means not letting her stand still, and a body that reads a room half a second ahead is very poor at being surprised by one. Against anything slower she wins before it commits. She has never once been in a fight and describes her own capability as a scheduling problem, which is the most accurate thing anybody has said about her.
notes: Every advantage here is paired with an authored cost, and both halves are the same fact rather than two rules: her speed is what releases her from every calendar and what prevents her from spending anything on her own schedule. The pairing is anatomical in its origin, in a fire-affinity body with no elemental seat beneath it, and institutional in its expression, in the exemption clause and the elixir method the setting already states are closed to her. No mechanic has been invented for her.
Her species carries an unset ceiling in the record. That is the absence of an authored ladder, not a ceiling of nothing, and this record writes the absence rather than supplying a number.

identity.realm: The ninth gate on the qi path. His line's wall is the seventeenth and it is arithmetic rather than effort: the density that makes a stoneborn the most durable body in the record is the density that will not let a dantian form the next one, and the species stops where the setting becomes layered, because a dense frame cannot be written into a second layer at all. He is a long way from that wall and has never once described himself as walking toward it.

appearance.presentation: A very large, very slow man who is always listening, and who has the particular look of somebody who has stopped moving because the ground said something. He reads as an instrument that has been stood in a field rather than as a man who walked into one.
appearance.age: Fifty-one. An ordinary span for a stoneborn and a short one for the density he carries, which buys him a long service and no hurry in any of it.
appearance.build: Enormous, dense and unhurried, carrying more physique and stamina than anything else on this side of the setting, and stopping short of the immortal tier for the same reason it carries the rest.
appearance.complexion: Grey-white mineral, faintly translucent at the ear, with a permanent grey bloom across the shoulders where he kneels on worked ground.
appearance.hair: None, the bare scalp finely fissured in the way this body's scalp always is, and kept shaved because nothing grows well on a frame that runs cold.
appearance.eyes: Slow to focus and wide, used to holding a distance rather than a face, and they go unfocused for long stretches while the rest of him is working.
appearance.palette: Field grey, ore dust, unbleached linen, and one band of dull brass at the wrist that belongs to the survey and not to him.
appearance.attire: A kneeling coat of grey and unbleached linen, hem bound with cord and cut to take the weight off a frame that cannot kneel cheaply, with a broad pad strapped over the right knee and the survey band at the wrist.
appearance.marks: Both knees worn to the same hard shine, a pale ridge of healed stone dust along the shin, and the specific callus of a man who puts his whole weight on a floor and waits there.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely still once he stops, which happens without warning and without any visible decision. People finish talking to his back and then wait.

canon.role_in_story: The Blind Survey holds that a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it, and the guild's whole professional ethic is built on that clause: no survey in this setting is finished until a second kind of sense has agreed with the first. A dense body transmits ground vibration better than anything else here, which makes him the finest sounding plate in the guild — and a use his own builders never claimed, because a body that stands on the ground and listens to it is not a tool anybody in the guild has paperwork for. So every reading he closes is closed provisionally, by definition and forever, because the next reading will reopen it; and he has never been paid a rate, qualified, or entered in a roll of instruments, because the guild cannot name what it is using. He has made a thirty-year career of being the last step of a method that is designed never to end, at a Cairn Field whose whole purpose is to certify breakthroughs that no tier here is licensed to attempt.
canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling on the Cairn Field with his weight entirely on one knee and one palm flat on the stone, eyes open and unfocused, not moving, while an assistant finished a reading he had already heard.
canon.lore:
A stoneborn is a dense, slow body assembled for load-bearing work. It carries more physique and stamina than anything else in this setting and it stops at the Immortal tier, because the density that makes it durable is the same density that will not let a dantian form. Mind cultivation is closed to the species outright. What the frame buys, beyond the obvious, is the one property nobody in the guild's history has had a use for: it transmits ground vibration better than anything else on the plains. A survey culture whose founding rule is that an eye reading is provisional until somebody has heard it has been running for generations on instruments that could not hear, and the finest instrument available has been standing in the field the whole time as a man kneeling on a pad.

That is the whole of his trade and it is genuinely strange, because the hearing cannot end the survey. The rule is not that a second sense confirms a first one; it is that until it has been heard the reading does not exist yet, which makes every confirmed reading provisional in the same breath, since the confirmation is itself a reading and therefore also provisional. He closes several hundred of them a season and none of them is closed. He is extremely good at this and has no qualification, no rate, no entry in any roll of instruments and no roster position at all, because the guild has never been willing to describe what it is using, and an office that will not describe a thing will not pay for it. The same body is also the setting's most valuable load on a spoil heap: there is exactly one job on the plains that cannot be done without being taught, and it is taught by the weight moved rather than by instruction, so the settlement's published figure for how much stone the ridge has left per unit of ground worked is measured in his shifts.

He is also the standing evidence in a dispute nobody wants settled. The densest bodies stop one gate short of the end of their own tier, and whoever benefits from an unexplained ceiling wants the hole shut. The disclosure that would close it is a disclosure about the densest body in the setting, and this species has never filed one. He has sat inside that gap for thirty years as a man who reads ground for a living and has never once filed what he reads about himself, and he has had the opportunity refused on his behalf twice by people who thought they were protecting the guild. The Gap School's method would settle it in an afternoon — seat a law, diff what the tier newly permits, move the student somewhere that law is missing — except that the final step is to move him, and a dense frame cannot be seated with the law that would let it leave its own frame. The method's last move is the one move his body cannot make.

What he does instead is the hardest watch in the rotation. A dense body stands a long watch better than anything else here, and the hours nobody volunteers for are the ones he has taken, every time, for thirty years. He does not claim to prefer it. He says the ground is quieter at that hour and that a quiet floor is easier to hear through, which is either true or the best reason he has found, and he has never offered the other one.
history: Was bred back toward flesh out of a mineral ancestor at a guild whose cold-bathing practice hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain, and kept a dantian when the practice was run one step further than intended.
Was sent to the Cairn Field at nineteen to carry slate and stayed because he could hear the ground through it, which nobody had thought to test for.
Closed his first reading at twenty-three and was told by the guild that a reading closed by an unlisted person is a reading not closed, which is true and which he has been living inside ever since.
Took the rotation's hardest watch in his twenties on the ground that a quiet floor is easier to hear through, and has taken it every season since.

Was offered a place at the Gap School twice and declined twice on the same ground both times: the method ends by moving the student somewhere a law is missing, and his frame cannot be seated with the law that would let it go.

reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to move him and do not expect him to be surprised; the frame does not tire and the first thing it does is put a hand on the floor. There is no technique that works on a body that arrives at full density every time and never once goes past. His weakness is entirely procedural: he cannot be made to act without a floor, he cannot be moved off one, and nobody has ever successfully improvised a situation in which those two facts were the same problem. He has been in exactly one fight and describes it as a bad survey.

identity.realm: The sixth gate on the qi path, and the sixth is roughly where the baseline stops being a baseline. Her species lends no discipline and stops where mortals stop: nothing about a commonborn's anatomy favours any of the three paths, so a Commonborn has to settle on one early and is weakest precisely at the rungs a specialist finds easy. The mind path is closed to her outright, because this body has no native faculty for it at all rather than because of anything she did.

appearance.presentation: An ordinary woman in a good coat, to the exact degree that ordinary is useful: she looks like the person any office would put on a form when it needed a body filled in quickly, and that is not an appearance she chose.
appearance.age: Sixty-one, on a species span that runs a century, which means she has already spent the part of a life in which a decision about a path could still have been cheap to change.
appearance.build: Unremarkable in every direction. Nothing about her frame favours one frame of work over another, which is why she is the setting's default and why no specialist ever has to say so out loud.
appearance.complexion: Warm common brown, weathered at the cheekbones by a life mostly spent outdoors, with the sun line across the nose of somebody who reads documents in daylight.
appearance.hair: Brown going grey at the temple, tied back in the plain knot that every house on the plains teaches its children before it teaches them anything else.
appearance.eyes: Steady, mid-brown, and trained to go flat on a document rather than to hold a person, which she can still do and does at will.
appearance.palette: Ledger cream, ink brown, road dust, and one inherited green thread at the collar that belongs to a household she no longer lives in.
appearance.attire: A good travelling coat of ledger cream gone grey at the elbows, a waxed satchel worn smooth on one side, and boots resoled twice by somebody else's cobbler.
appearance.marks: A hard callus on the middle finger of her right hand from a pen held too hard for thirty years, and a pale line at each wrist where the satchel strap has cut.
appearance.bearing: Square, unhurried and eminently substitutable. She stands where she has been put and does not adjust it, which reads as modesty and functions as availability.

canon.role_in_story: Every institution in this setting wants a body it has not had to qualify, and a commonborn is that body: nothing about the frame favours a path, so any of the three traditions can take her and none of them has a reason to refuse. That is why every office she has ever walked into has found a place for her, and it is why none of them has ever kept one past the term it was created for. She reached the sixth gate by being the person who was always available to be trained, which is a statement about the setting's appetite rather than about her, and she has stopped correcting people who read it as a compliment. On the qi path she is strongest on the floor rung, where nobody is a specialist yet, and weakest on every rung above it, because the ladder asks for a specialisation her anatomy declines to supply and will not supply later. The mind path is closed to her outright and has nothing to do with her choice: this body has no native faculty for it, which is exactly what a deadlight's restored interior proves by contrast.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in a registrar's queue holding a form she had already filled in for the person in front of her, and being asked to hold the next one.
canon.lore:
A commonborn is the body everyone is born into before the world has an opinion about them. It stops where mortals stop and lends no discipline, which is exactly why it is weak: nothing about its anatomy favours a path, so a commonborn has to settle on one early and is weakest precisely where a specialist is strongest. Mind is closed to it outright, because this body has no native faculty for the mind path at all. The subspecies that replaced a lanternfolk's fungal colony with a mineral bloom gained that path back in the same frame that lost two hundred and fifty years, and the pair is the proof that commonborn's closed path is caused by the absence of a cause rather than by its own anatomy — which means her exclusion is not an anatomy at all. It is a missing thing, and the record has nothing further to say about who removed it.

She settled on qi at fourteen, which is early enough that the decision was made before she could have been informed by it, and she has been the sixth gate ever since. The qi ladder asks each rung for something more particular than the last, and every particularity it asks for is a specialisation, and the one resource she does not have is a preference. What she has instead is availability: she can be trained by anyone, at any time, by any of the three traditions, which in a setting where nobody licenses anybody is worth more than it looks and exactly what is worth less than it looks. A registry will put a body on a form without checking, a school will seat a student without a qualification, a household will hand her the work nobody wants — and every one of those arrangements is a substitution, and none of them is a tenure.

The School of the Closed Frame holds that the universe is a closed budget and that every doctrine of a seventh group is an arithmetic error rather than a mystery. She is the cheapest possible argument against it, because she is what the six written groups produce when they have nobody in mind: entirely ordinary, entirely produced, and unable to reach the top of the cheapest of the three ladders. The Gap School's method would say she is the perfect subject, since it teaches by seating a law, diffing what the tier newly permits, and then moving the student somewhere that law is missing — and she is a body with no seat of her own, so she is the one student in the setting who can be moved without cost.

She weighs rather than quotes. The Standing Weight is a second currency that refuses to state a price and lets nobody make the first offer, and for most of this setting that concealment is administrative. For her it is anatomical: she is the only body in the setting with no affinity, no resonance, no frame signature and nothing whatever that a scale could betray, which makes her the one person a weighed transaction cannot read. She has been put on a scale by four institutions in her life and has never once been asked what she weighs, because the answer was never the question, and she has never been able to establish what the question was.
history: Was settled on the qi path at fourteen by a household that needed the decision settled, which is the ordinary use of an ordinary body and the only thing she was asked to contribute to it.
Trained at the Gap School at nineteen, because a body with no seat of her own is the one student who can be moved to wherever a law is missing, and was moved four times in six years.
Has been trained by three traditions in her life and has never refused any of them, which is the strongest thing anybody can say about her and the weakest thing she can say about herself.

Was entered on a registry roll as an unnamed body to fill a form and discovered she had been entered under the wrong year, which nobody corrected because correcting it would have required a line that did not exist.
Was refused at the seventh gate for want of a qualification and told, kindly, that the question did not arise for bodies like hers.

relationships.note: The frame everyone is born into before the world has an opinion about them: it stops where mortals stop, lends no discipline, and is weak precisely where a specialist is strong, because nothing in its anatomy favours a path and a commonborn must settle on one early. Her whole career is the shape of that sentence, and she has made no attempt to argue with it.

A lanternfolk lineage whose colony died and whose wound was colonised by a mineral bloom lost two hundred and fifty years and got the mind path back in the same frame. That is the control case: the closed mind path in her own body is caused by the absence of a cause rather than by her anatomy, which means her exclusion is a missing thing and not a property. She has been told this by nobody and has worked it out herself.

An academy that teaches by seating a law, diffing what the tier newly permits, and then moving the student somewhere that law is missing. A body with no seat of its own is the perfect subject for that method and the only one it can use freely, so she was moved four times in six years and every move was someone else's decision and nobody's expense.

Weigh, never quote, and let nobody make the first offer, because a buyer who names a figure first forfeits standing. For most of the setting that concealment is administrative. Hers is anatomical: no affinity, no resonance, no frame signature, nothing a scale could betray — the one person a weighed transaction cannot read, and the only one who has therefore never been told what she weighs.

The school holds that the universe is a closed budget and that every doctrine of a seventh group is an arithmetic error rather than a mystery. She is what the six written groups produce when they have nobody in mind: entirely ordinary, entirely produced, and unable to reach the top of the cheapest of the three ladders. The school finds her uninteresting, which is the most expensive thing it has ever done.

A mortuary college that reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, and records the divergence rather than resolving it. She is alive and on its working rolls and was entered as an unnamed body to fill a form, under a year that was wrong, and nobody corrected it because correcting it would have required a line that did not exist.

reference_stats.combat_read: There is no reading to fear and no rhythm to break. She has no signature for an instrument to lock onto, no burst to time and no reserve to exhaust, so the usual answers do not apply and the fight becomes a question of how long the opponent is willing to keep choosing a target that cannot be predicted. She fights by not being the shape you prepared for, and has won exactly one encounter, which she describes as the other person leaving.

aliases: one gate, one measure of old water

identity.realm: Qi Refining: the first gate of the qi ladder, opened once, seated on a floor she cut herself at the old waterline. It is the most ordinary rung in this setting and the one no saltwrack had ever touched, because all three of her species' paths are complete and none has ever been exercised at any scale. She is not the first of anything. She is the first.

appearance.presentation: A thin woman from the wasted side of a waterline, salt-crusted from the knee down and carrying herself with the specific caution of somebody who knows exactly how far past the edge of the brine she is standing. She reads as a person who has been told to be careful her whole life and has never once been told why.
appearance.age: Thirty-one, on a saltfolk span that runs over a century, which means her whole life fits inside one run of a basin that has already failed three times.
appearance.build: Gracile and light-boned and slightly underfed in a way that reads as poverty until you learn it reads as chemistry: what the basin still grows is not enough for a body built to need brine, and everything it does grow has had its usefulness taken out of it.
appearance.complexion: Pale and faintly frosted, with the hardened dermal crust that runs up from the ankles over her lifetime and is now thicker on the left shin than the right, because she works that side.
appearance.hair: Bleached to straw in long uneven streaks where the crust has grown through it, and cut off blunt above the shoulder because a saltfolk's hair mats with salt and takes a season to come out.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and tired at the rims, with the flat unremarkable vision of her species — taste is the instrument and vision is not, so she looks at everything and reads nothing.
appearance.palette: Crust white, dried brine grey, faded indigo of an old crossing coat, and the black mineral line that marks the waterline she was born above.
appearance.attire: A short crossing coat of faded indigo gone stiff with salt, bound at the waist with cord, over wrapped leggings heavy with dried crust; the hem is cut high because it has never been dry since she was given it.
appearance.marks: The black mineral line at each ankle where the old waterline sat on her skin, and two shallow healed splits at the heel from a floor cut badly in stone.
appearance.bearing: Low, careful and quick on level ground, stopping dead at any change in the ground's colour, because for her body the colour of the ground is the only reading there is.

canon.role_in_story: Her lineage's brine was replaced rather than drained, so everything it was built to drink became poison to it and everything it could tolerate became nutritionally empty; three generations of famine took the rest, and nobody hunted her people, because there is nothing here of the usual kind of extinction. One element moved. What remains is a population whose only method for continuing is the sealed sump of the old concentration on the basin floor, and there is one sump. She is the first of her species to have sat a gate, and the reason she sits the most ordinary rung in the setting is that the ordinary rung was available: all three of her paths are complete and none has ever been exercised at any scale, so there was nothing to copy and nothing to catch up with. She cut a floor in stone at the old waterline and sat on it. The cost was measured in the only unit her species still has, and she has not decided whether the gate was worth it, because the same measure is what a child would need and there is one of it.
canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling on a stone shelf cut into the basin wall with her palm flat on the rock, tasting the air above the old line, and refusing to move until somebody finished waiting.
canon.lore:
A saltfolk body was rebuilt for brine no softer body could drink: extraordinary renal mass, a brine sac running dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine that splits the penetrating vessel into two halves which cannot be rejoined, a hardened dermal salt crust, and flat teeth for grinding crust rather than sharp ones for tearing. They read brine concentration across four orders of dilution by taste, where a human nose finds them sour. Total dependence on the supply is the whole of the bargain, and a saltfolk carried onto fresh ground is already dying: nine days above the line, and no cultivation repairs it. That is why they are a species of a resource rather than a nation of one, and why the dominion whose territory is exactly its waterline needs no administration to stay put.

On this basin the element moved rather than vanished. The brine was diluted and replaced, so the water their kidneys were built to concentrate is now poison to them, and the crust they could grind has been rinsed of everything a salt body needs from it. They were never hunted. There is no predator in this account and no raid and no plague; what happened was a change of concentration, and a population with no alternative to one dissolved element had nothing left. Three generations of famine took the rest, which is the single largest cause of longwinter infant loss in a different species and here simply the end. What survives is viable only while one sealed sump holds the previous concentration, and the sump is the only thing on this basin worth anything.

The arithmetic of that is not a metaphor. A saltfolk zygote carries a brine load from conception and a dry birth kills the infant — which is why the culture binds every child to a named debt before first breath is drawn cold. The saltwrack condition runs the other way: the load is now poison, so a birth needs the old concentration available at the moment of it, and the only old concentration in existence is in a container with a finite volume. Every child this lineage will ever have is a withdrawal from that container. That is the whole of the debt line for a body of this kind, and it is not a figure of speech; it is the same container, drawn down once for a gate and once for a child, and there is no third thing it can be spent on.

So she cut a floor in the stone at the old line and opened the first gate of her species' qi ladder on it, which is the most ordinary rung in this setting — the one every beginner sits and the one a brinecaller's widened range would also reach. She did it because the ordinary rung was the only one nobody could charge her for advice about. The setting's remaining debates about her people are all arguments: whether the waterline is a border or a measurement, who owns a depth, whether a stranded population that never exercised any path still has a claim. She has answered none of them and produced one fact instead, which is that a clade whose three paths are all complete can take the first gate, and that the price of the first gate was drawn from the only thing she had.
history: Was born on the wasted side of the waterline into the third generation after the brine was replaced, into a household that had already lost its fertile years to chemistry rather than to anything anybody did.
Learned to taste the brine against the sump's seal before she could read, because her mother's hands were the only instrument the household had and the hands were failing.
Was bound to a named debt before first breath was drawn cold, on the ordinary rule, which for a body of hers means a claim against a container rather than against a person.

Cut a stone floor at the old waterline at twenty-six, on the reasoning that the first gate of her species' path was the one nobody could charge her advice for, and seated it there without an office and without a chart.
Spent the measure on the gate before anybody had agreed that a gate was worth a measure, and has not been able to establish since whether that was a trade or a mistake.

relationships.note: A saltfolk lineage stranded on one basin whose brine was replaced rather than lost: everything built to drink became poison and everything it could tolerate became nutritionally empty. They were never hunted — there is no predator, no raid and no plague in the account, only one element moving — and a species with no alternative to one dissolved element had nothing left. Her first gate is the first fact any of them has ever produced.

The parent population continues to sell access to a resource that has already destroyed one of its own lineages without anyone changing its price. Their brine sac splits the penetrating vessel at the eleventh gate, which is their ceiling and not hers; what she has instead is a body that cannot drink what it is standing beside, and the parent goes on trading across the line every season.

Every child is bound to a named debt before first breath is drawn cold, because a line held pure inside one household concentrates faster, and this is the sharpest version of that logic anywhere in the setting: a saltfolk zygote carries a brine load from conception and a dry birth kills it. Her condition runs the other way, so her binding is a claim against the one sealed measure of old concentration that still exists, and the debt line for her is a siphon rather than a contract.

Whether the waterline is a border or a measurement, and whether a stranded population that never exercised any path still holds a claim. She has made no argument and filed nothing. She sat the first gate of her species' ladder on a floor she cut herself, which is not a claim and is not rhetoric, and it is the only evidence in the dispute that the unexercised paths are complete rather than theoretical.

A crossing that widened the range and left the eleventh-realm ceiling exactly where the salt parent had it, which would have let a body drink both sides of a boundary that a dominion's whole argument depends on being untestable. The parent population never adopted it. She has cited it once, in a basin, to nobody, and the sump has outlasted the argument.

The first gate of the energy ladder: prepare a reservoir and sit it. A gate a few hundred practitioners clear every year and the one a species that has never touched its own path can therefore take with nothing to copy. She seated it on a floor cut in stone at the old waterline with no office present and no chart to enter it on, and paid for it out of the same measure a birth would need.

reference_stats.summary: The first practitioner of a clade that had never exercised any path, sitting the first rung of the cheapest ladder in the setting. Her capability is modest and her position is not available to anybody else.

reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight her on a shoreline and do not believe she is helpless in one. She cannot leave the brine line and has never been in a fight, and she has been correctly described in both cases by people who never had to test the first claim. Any opponent who wants her dead must stand where the ground changes colour, because that is the only ground her body reads and the only ground on which she can be made to move without warning her.
notes: Every advantage is paired with an authored cost and the pairing is anatomical: the taste that reads four orders of dilution is the same organ system that makes fresh water poison, and the completeness of her three paths is the reason she had nothing to copy and no specialist to train beside. Both halves come out of the species record as written; nothing has been added for her.

The species is recorded with an authored ceiling at the eleventh gate and with the note that a saltwrack ladder was never exercised at any scale, so her realm is stated as the first rung taken and the absence of any authored ordinal above it is left as an absence.

identity.realm: The eleventh gate on the qi path, and reached late, which for his species is the method rather than a shortfall in it: longwinter qi accumulates rather than circulates, so a breakthrough arrives when the reserve is full and not before, and their breakthroughs are late and rarely fail. His line's wall is the seventeenth, the first gate needing two flank vessels held at once, and a longwinter has one warm gradient, briefly, in summer. He has described the eleven as the shape of his job and has never described it as an approach.

appearance.presentation: A broad, low, unhurried man with the settled heaviness of somebody who is already carrying next winter, and who treats the present as the cheap half of the year. He reads as furniture that has been in the room longer than the room.
appearance.age: Fifty-two. A longwinter span runs past a century, which means he has done rather less with his life than his face suggests and has banked more of it than anyone in the room.
appearance.build: Broad and low with heavy subcutaneous fat, a lowered cold-tolerant core and reduced limb length: a frame shaped for a winter of dormancy rather than for anything that has to be carried quickly.
appearance.complexion: Pale and waxy in cold light, deepening in warm, with the mottling that a body keeps when its own temperature is the thing being negotiated.
appearance.hair: Thick, dark and worn long, because a longwinter's hair is thick and the reason to cut it is heat rather than fashion, and he has not spent a summer hot enough to want it.
appearance.eyes: Small, dark and patient, with the slight unfocus of a body whose core runs cold, and a way of looking at a person as though the person would still be there.
appearance.palette: Hide brown, peat black, undyed wool, and the pale grey of frost that never quite leaves the seams of anything he owns.
appearance.attire: Layered hide and undyed wool to the throat, seams bound with waxed cord, a charter-house licence sewn inside the left shoulder where only he can reach it, and boots turned down at the top for standing in cold.
appearance.marks: A broad unbroken band of pale skin across both knuckles, and the flattened soles of somebody who has walked cold ground for forty years without hurrying.
appearance.bearing: Low, unhurried and immovable, with the specific heaviness of somebody who is already carrying a decision they have not announced. Rooms settle around him because he is the warmest thing in them and the least urgent.

canon.role_in_story: Qi accumulates in his species rather than circulating, so a longwinter's breakthrough arrives when the reserve is full and not on any chosen day, and their breakthroughs are late and rarely fail. That single physiological fact makes his cultivation and his hibernation the same discipline: he packs a winter as fat, and the same packing is what the qi ladder is asking him for, and the only technique in this setting built to make a breakthrough happen at a chosen moment assumes a body that circulates fast enough to be timed. He is the setting's best long-haul body, and the reason is the same fact that makes him slow: a winter is an asset to a frame that treats it as one, and a liability to one that does not. So he carries things. That is his trade, that is his skill, and it has left him in a house whose real fortune is in what its porters can keep moving, which is the only economy in this setting that pays a longwinter for being exactly what he is and asks nothing of him that he has not already been built to do.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in a road house doorway in the last week before the passes closed, unhurried, with a load already off his shoulders and no intention of leaving until the thaw.
canon.lore:
A longwinter is built on a hibernate-and-store cycle: it packs a winter as body fat rather than as qi, and that single decision puts the flank vessels out of reach, because those vessels need two warm gradients held at once and a longwinter has one, briefly, in summer. On qi the path is complete and slow — the same cycle that stores fat stores qi. The soul is seated very deep and very quiet, which makes it difficult to read and exceptionally hard to damage, and qi accumulates rather than circulates, so breakthroughs are late and rarely fail. They reach far and never stay there, which is exactly why they are the setting's best long-haul traders: a frame that banks rather than circulates is a frame that can be loaded in August and is still carrying in March.

What that produces, in a setting whose institutions are all built around circulating bodies, is a practitioner with a very specific failure. Almost nothing here can be done at a chosen moment. The first purchasable technique is a dose timed to the tide that will carry it, on a stone bed that holds qi — a method that sells preparation rather than attempt, and that is worth nothing below its own tier because a tide cannot be read on many frames. A frame that accumulates rather than circulates cannot be timed by a tide in the first place, because there is nothing circulating to be carried by it. He has never wanted the method and has never been able to buy it, and he has stopped finding that interesting, because he does not need a tide: he needs eleven weeks of summer and a warm enough room, and then he arrives at the gate on the day the reserve is full. He has not missed a gate he ever began. He has begun rather fewer than anyone who has watched him.

His species' ceiling is arithmetic rather than effort and it is the same wall this setting's layered law puts in front of any body that cannot be written into a second layer: two flank vessels, held at once, and one warm gradient a year. He is at the eleventh. He was at the ninth for a decade and describes the wait as the shape of his job, not as a wall, because a body that banks has a different relationship with delay than one that circulates: delay is not time wasted, it is the medium the work happens in.

He carries. The road houses he works out of treat a short-lived body as the most valuable guest they have and the one they are worst at losing, and treat a long-lived one as the reverse, and neither of those judgements is quite the truth: a furnace body that goes out on the road costs a house a customer and a creditor at once, while a long-haul body that fails does so slowly enough to put down first. He is also the reason the setting's oldest migration has a footnote. The answer to the Iron Grief was to leave for the Spirit Peaks, and a long-haul body is the one population that could make that journey on a single load, and the only one that cannot be hurried into it, and the crossing was made by carriers who were told to go and then went at whatever pace the snow allowed.
history: Was left at a road house at nine with a load and a licence sewn inside his shoulder, on the practice that a long-haul body is worth more started young than argued about at sixteen.
Walked his first full crossing in his twenties and arrived with the load intact, which is the only test the trade applies to a body and the only credential he has ever needed.
Opened his first qi gate at thirty-four, after a decade of banking and one warm room, and has never failed to open a gate he began.

Was offered a channel elixir and a seat on a spirit stone bed by a house that wanted his crossings faster, and declined both, having worked out that a body which accumulates rather than circulates is the one frame the method was never for.

Stopped at the ninth for a decade and called the wait his job rather than a wall, and has said since that the eleventh arrived the same way every gate has: in the summer, when the reserve was full and nobody was asking.

personality.summary: Unhurried to a point that other people read as slowness and that is in fact the only tempo at which he can be relied on. He makes decisions the way his body makes warmth: slowly, early, and then not at all again for months.

relationships.note: A cold-climate body on a hibernate-and-store cycle that packs a winter as fat rather than as qi, which puts the flank vessels out of reach because they need two warm gradients held at once and this body has one, briefly, in summer. Qi accumulates rather than circulates, so the breakthroughs are late and rarely fail, and the species reaches far and never stays there — which is precisely what makes it the best long-haul body in the setting and precisely what makes it useless at anything with a date attached.

Road houses treat a short-lived body as their most valuable guest and the one they are worst at losing, and treat a long-lived one as the reverse; the truer reading is that a furnace body that fails on the road costs a house a customer and a creditor at once, while a long-haul body fails slowly enough to set the load down first. He has been the difference between those two losses for forty years and has never been the difference between anything else.

The flank vessels are the wall: they need two simultaneous pressure sources where a body fed by one resonator has one, and for his species the same gate needs two warm gradients held at once where a longwinter has one for eleven weeks in summer. His eleventh is not an approach to it and he has never described it as one — the two are different pieces of arithmetic and only one of them is an attainment.

Prepare a reservoir and sit it: the floor of the ladder, and the one rung whose own instruction — hold — is the instruction his whole physiology has been running since he was born. He took it at thirty-four after a decade of banking and has never failed to take anything he began, which is a rate nobody can distinguish from luck until you learn that he does not begin very often.

The first purchasable technique prepares a breakthrough by a dose timed to the tide that will carry it, on a stone bed that holds qi. He has declined it and could not have afforded it, because there is nothing circulating in his frame for a tide to carry — the reserve banks. The offer that came with it was his crossings made faster, which is the one thing his frame cannot do, and he worked that out in the time it took to be asked.

The answer to the Iron Grief was to leave for the Spirit Peaks. A long-haul body is the one population that could make that journey on a single load and also the only one that cannot be hurried into it, so the crossing was made by carriers who were told to go and then went at whatever pace the snow allowed, and the record counts it as a migration rather than a flight.

reference_stats.summary: A body that banks rather than circulates, so it arrives late, arrives intact, and cannot be asked to arrive sooner. Nothing in this setting can time him and nothing in this setting can make him late for a load.
strengths: qi accumulates rather than circulates, so he has never failed to open a gate he began, which is a reliability no circulating body in the record can claim
the best long-haul frame on this tier: loaded in one season and still carrying in the third, and it fails slowly enough to set the load down first
a soul seated very deep and very quiet, difficult to read and exceptionally hard to damage
carries a full season's work and does not tire, hurry or reconsider, which is worth more on a road than any technique
weaknesses: cannot attempt anything at a chosen moment, so any date can be refused to him and he has no way to argue with the refusal
one warm gradient a year where the seventeenth gate needs two at once, so his ceiling is physiological rather than a matter of discipline
every capability he has expires on arrival, so nothing he does outlasts his usefulness to whoever was carrying it
his speed is the same fact as his reliability, and there is no arrangement in the setting that pays for reliability without asking for speed
his species' whole cycle assumes a real winter, and a warm year is a bad year and a warm decade is a catastrophe
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no opening to exploit and no burst to time, because he has no burst and no opening: he banks, and the exchange is decided by who was willing to start without a reserve. Anything that requires him to respond inside a window will win, because a body that accumulates cannot answer inside one. Anything that requires him to still be standing at the end will not, because he has never in his life been the kind of body that runs out. He has been in two fights and declined a third on the grounds that the road was going to be there in the spring.
notes: Every advantage is paired with an authored cost and the pairing here is the same physiological fact in both directions: the accumulation that makes his breakthroughs late and rarely fail is what makes him untimeable, and the winter he can treat as an asset is a winter the frame needs two of. Both halves are in the species record as written, and no mechanic has been added for him.
The longwinter ceiling is authored at the seventeenth gate with a stated mechanism, so this record names the ordinal and its cause rather than implying one.
